extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants for the NEH Public Scholar Program (humanities authors, affiliated and independent scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting proposals for the NEH Public Scholar Program, which funds well-researched humanities books intended for broad general readerships. Includes eligibility notes about applicant affiliation and project stage and describes the kinds of books and qualities the program seeks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience scope — broad readership
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports well-researched books in the humanities intended to reach a broad readership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program aims to encourage scholarship that will be of broad interest and have lasting impact; the challenge is to make sense of a significant topic in a way that will appeal to general readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounding in humanities research and scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: Books supported by this program must be grounded in humanities research and scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making use of primary and/or secondary sources is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects must address significant humanities themes likely to be of broad interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant themes are those that deepen understanding of the human condition, current conditions, or contemporary problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible writing style
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects must be written in a readily accessible style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should craft prose and presentation that open up important and appealing subjects for wider audiences; avoid overly specialized or inaccessible scholarly language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Project should make use of primary and/or secondary sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly grounding via appropriate sources demonstrates research rigor and supports the book's claims and narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended intellectual contribution or approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The program seeks scholarship that presents meaningful intellectual contributions in forms accessible to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such scholarship might present a narrative history, tell the stories of important individuals, analyze significant texts, provide a synthesis of ideas, revive interest in a neglected subject, or examine the latest thinking on a topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for lasting impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects should be likely to have lasting impact beyond immediate publicity or transient interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEH emphasizes scholarship that deepens public understanding and remains relevant over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant/project stage eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH especially welcomes applicants who are in the writing stages of their projects or who already have a commitment from a publisher, but the program also supports projects in the early stages of development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants at different stages (early development to in-progress writing) may be eligible; having a publisher commitment is helpful but not strictly required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant affiliation eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is open to both individuals affiliated with scholarly institutions and independent scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both institution-affiliated and independent applicants may apply; contact NEH staff for accessibility accommodations (e.g., TDD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural/timing requirement (example cycle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt deadline and project start timing are specified (example: Receipt Deadline March 3, 2015 for Projects Beginning October 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow the program's published deadlines and project start windows for each competition; consult current guidelines and application materials for the applicable cycle.
